answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds agent identities to cryptographic stake burning via a quadratic staking pool. When rogue entities wander into the protocol to multiply their presence, each added identity enforces superlinear cost scaling: creating k identities requires burning O(k^2) stake tokens, turning any attempted attacker echo into an exponential financial drain. Even a lightweight sparrow bot must commit irreversible value to participate.
